mentions.note: Buy now pay later company with a tremendous story for a while.
Long-term outperformer with Lisa Su challenging Nvidia at its own game. Cramer owns it.
Stock jumped nearly 10% to an all-time high on a terrific upside surprise, and Wall Street liked its frugal capex approach.
Upending law enforcement with tasers, body cameras, drones and AI-generated police reports. Cramer owns it.
Has the best consumer data, and the analyst day should tell a sanguine story about the economy. Very inexpensive stock.
Terrific company but Buffett is irreplaceable, and more profit-taking is expected as he steps down; Greg Abel takes over at year end.
One of the market's best performers, and the move is justified by equipment demand for building and maintaining data centers. Cramer thinks it is multi-year.
One of the year's best performers with clean nuclear power generation. Winners win, so keep buying.
Stock is down more than 30% YTD and sits at the heart of the consumer-staples conundrum, with shoppers refusing to pay up for name brands.
Lowest level since 2016 with green shoots in Europe and China, and a strong balance sheet. US tariffs remain a headwind.
At 45x earnings, Cramer says you can start a position; best in its industry and hurt by a magazine piece. His charitable trust owns it.
Bell cow of this rally that has won over millions of investors. Cramer expects fantastic numbers.
Strong Q3 beat, new CEO Kirk Tanner and conservative guidance set up upside, and the stock is probably near a bottom. Tempting starter position for those who believe in Tanner.
Doing amazing things in quantum, and the Trump administration's urgency on beating China should help IBM lead the way.
Down over 100 points on capex fears, but Zuckerberg's spending defends Meta's social dominance against OpenAI and rivals. Market has been wrong on Meta many times.
Better company than its stock price suggests and a great opportunity for advertisers, but it has not worked out and is not delivering, which Cramer called unacceptable.
Rare earth materials company with a tremendous story for a while.
Tremendous company at 24x earnings, but the move has been parabolic and Cramer would like to see it cool off.
Trades like a bond equivalent, with a 7% yield that appears safe and is backed by cash flow. Cramer wants to see if it can break out above $25.
Expects some profit-taking around earnings after the run, but is not backing away long term. Clients love the company and it is too good to ignore.
CEO Baratz is very good and the company reports this week, but Cramer prefers IBM in quantum.
Strong Q3 beat with 4% same-store sales growth, and 70% of cash flow from Canada and international. Long-term investors are rewarded, and short-term trading risks missing the next run.
A good speculative stock, but it loses so much money that Cramer would endorse it only as a spec.
Very reliable winner and an e-commerce champion serving small and medium-sized businesses.
Great story but a huge, parabolic run; Cramer does not like to recommend stocks in parabola mode.
Pure speculation; it has come down from its high but does not make money, and Cramer needs profitability before getting behind it.
A scrum among AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile makes for too many crosscurrents, so stay away.
New CEO has not yet made his imprint and the stock is out of favor. Cramer would rather own Costco for growth than Target's big yield.
Doing well and fulfilling its grand ambitions.
Stock is at arbitrage levels on takeover anticipation. A deal could add a couple more dollars, but without one it could fall sharply.
Lagging fast-food chain. Losers keep losing, and superior restaurant brands are available elsewhere.
